newsitem.title: USA: Horizon Group sees '97 FFO, AFFO below '96.
newsitem.headline: Horizon Group sees '97 FFO, AFFO below '96.

text.p: Horizon Group Inc said on Wednesday it expects its funds from operations and adjusted funds from operations in 1997 to be "significantly less" than those posted in 1996.
For the year ended December 31, funds from operations were $66.4 million, or $2.52 per share, versus $47.7 million, or $2.57 per share.
In 1996, adjusted funds from operations were $57.2 million, or $2.17 per share, compared to $42.6 million, or $2.30 per share.
The company said the projected drop is largely the result of costs associated with its Dole Cannery project in Honolulu, Hawaii.
In the fourth quarter, the company posted write-downs of $61.7 million.
Cost overruns and limited success in leasing its Dole Cannery project required a write-down of its investment in the project and a reserve against a related receivable, it said.
Horizon said that beginning in 1997, it will expense and not capitalise any costs incurred on the project, including lease, interest and operating costs.
In the fourth quarter of 1996, interest and operating expenses of $1.2 million were capitalised and are included in the write-down.

Although cash lease payments due on the lease in 1997 are $3.2 million, straight line lease expense accrued for financial reporting purposes will be $8 million for 1997 and a similar amount will be required to be accrued for each remaining year of the lease, the company said.

Horizon said it defines AFFO as net income before minority interest, excluding: gains or losses from real estate sales or debt restructuring, certain other one-time charges and write-downs, depreciation of real estate, and amortisation other than the amortisation of deferred financing cost.
